symbols.name: vector space
symbols.meaning: The vector space on which the linear operator T acts, over the field F.
symbols.quote: Here $V$, $\theta$ and $e$ denote a vector space, an eigenvalue and an eigenvector, whatever they denote elsewhere.

symbols.name: eigenvalue
symbols.meaning: A scalar for which T maps some nonzero vector e to the multiple theta e.
symbols.quote: Here $V$, $\theta$ and $e$ denote a vector space, an eigenvalue and an eigenvector, whatever they denote elsewhere.

symbols.name: eigenvector
symbols.meaning: A nonzero vector of V that T maps to a multiple of itself.
symbols.quote: Here $V$, $\theta$ and $e$ denote a vector space, an eigenvalue and an eigenvector, whatever they denote elsewhere.

symbols.name: rational numbers
symbols.quote: Here $\mathbb{Q}$ denotes the rational numbers, $\mathbb{Q}^h$ the vectors with $h$ rational entries, and $h\ge 2$ their number of coordinates.

symbols.name: coordinate count
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of each vector in Q^h, at least 2.
symbols.quote: Here $\mathbb{Q}$ denotes the rational numbers, $\mathbb{Q}^h$ the vectors with $h$ rational entries, and $h\ge 2$ their number of coordinates.

symbols.name: bilinear value
symbols.meaning: The number that the bilinear form assigns to the pair of vectors x and y.
symbols.quote: A bilinear form on $\mathbb{Q}^h$ assigns to vectors $x,y$ a number $\langle x,y\rangle$, linear in each argument.

symbols.name: transpose
symbols.meaning: The transpose of a column vector x, the row with the same entries.
symbols.quote: Here $x^{\mathsf T}$ is the row with the entries of $x$.

symbols.name: all-one matrix
symbols.meaning: The h by h matrix with every entry equal to 1.
symbols.quote: Let $J$ be the $h\times h$ matrix with every entry $1$.

symbols.name: all-ones vector
symbols.meaning: The vector in Q^h with every entry equal to 1.

symbols.name: average entry
symbols.meaning: The average of the entries of x, which is the coefficient of the all-ones vector in its split.
symbols.quote: Every $x$ in $\mathbb{Q}^h$ splits uniquely as $x=c\mathbf 1+x_0$, with $c$ the average entry of $x$ and $x_0$ summing to zero.

symbols.name: zero-sum part
symbols.meaning: The part of x whose entries sum to zero in the split x = c 1 + x_0.
symbols.quote: Every $x$ in $\mathbb{Q}^h$ splits uniquely as $x=c\mathbf 1+x_0$, with $c$ the average entry of $x$ and $x_0$ summing to zero.
